transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I... I guess I’m here because I can’t really shake this heavy feeling. It’s like after the divorce, everything I tried to build back up just... collapsed, and I’m stuck under it. It feels pretty hopeless.
How long have you been feeling this way?
About a month, I think. It kind of started when the financial stuff after the divorce got really messy. Since then it’s just… been there.
Do you find yourself enjoying things you used to like before the divorce?
I’m not really sure. I guess I don’t... think about those things much lately. Nothing really stands out.
Are there things that you still find pleasure in doing?
I don’t know... not really. I haven’t noticed anything lately that feels enjoyable.
Have you had any thoughts about harming yourself?
Yeah... I have. Not exactly like... I don't know. I've been thinking it might be easier if I just didn't wake up. It got bad enough that I scared myself and called the employee assistance program.
Have you noticed any changes in your energy level or how you're moving compared to before you started feeling this way?
Yeah... my energy’s been really low. Getting through a normal workday feels like dragging wet concrete. Even small things, like showering or opening my laptop, feel like more than I have in me.
Have you experienced any strange thoughts or heard voices that others couldn't hear since you've been feeling this way?
No... I don’t think so. I haven’t heard anything like that, or had thoughts that felt... strange in that way.
Do you feel like you're moving slower than usual or have trouble sitting still?

I guess… more restless than slow. I’d pace around my apartment when there wasn’t even anything useful left to do. And I kept pushing myself into extra work stuff—proposals, calling people with ideas, volunteering for things no one asked me to take on.
Have you noticed any changes in your weight since you started feeling this way?
Not really... I haven’t been keeping close track. My clothes feel about the same, I think.
Have you thought about how you would do it if you decided to harm yourself?
No… I didn’t have, like, a specific plan. It was more… thinking it might be easier if I just didn’t wake up. It got intense enough that I scared myself and called the employee assistance program.
Have you lost a significant amount of weight since you started feeling this way?
No, I don’t think so. I haven’t really noticed any big weight change.
Have you thought about or come up with a specific way to harm yourself?
No… not a specific way. It was more like… thinking it’d be easier if I just didn’t wake up. It got bad enough that it scared me, so I called the employee assistance program.
Have you made any preparations to harm yourself?
No… I didn’t make preparations or anything like that. It was more just… those thoughts about not waking up. They scared me enough that I called the employee assistance program.
Do you feel worse in the morning?

I don’t know if it’s specifically worse in the morning. It’s more just… this heavy, hopeless feeling that’s there when I wake up. Like everything I tried to rebuild after my divorce has kind of collapsed, and I’m stuck under it.
Do you feel like you're unable to experience any pleasure at all?
I’m not sure I’d say “unable to feel anything at all.” It’s more like… things just don’t really reach me much right now. I don’t get much out of them.
Do you feel like your low mood is present most of the day?
Yeah… most of the day. It’s just this heavy, hopeless feeling I can’t really shake, like everything I’d put back together after the divorce has fallen in on me.
Do you feel like your low mood is significantly worse than a normal sadness?
Yeah… it feels a lot worse than just normal sadness. It’s more like this heavy, hopeless feeling I can’t get out from under. Like everything I’d built back up after the divorce just… collapsed.
Do you feel like you've lost interest in activities you used to enjoy?
I don’t know… maybe. I haven’t really been paying close attention to it. Things just feel kind of flat.
Do you feel like your current state is significantly interfering with your daily life?

Yeah. It’s… it’s been pretty bad. I was making poor calls at work and kind of falling apart in meetings, so my supervisor pulled me off active project decisions.

And at home I’m not really keeping up with basic things. It got to the point where I was sent to the emergency department because I didn’t feel safe with my thoughts.
Do you feel like your low mood is as bad as it can be?
It feels close to that, yeah. I came in because I just… I can’t shake this heavy, hopeless feeling. Like everything I built back up after the divorce collapsed, and I’m just stuck under it.
